source: Body systems work together. Bones hold you up and muscles move them. The heart pumps blood; the lungs bring in oxygen; the stomach and intestines break down food; the brain and nerves send messages.
Thinking the heart is on the far left of the chest and shaped like a valentine. It is near the middle, tipped a little to the left, and about the size of your fist.
Your body is made of systems, teams of parts that work together. They all have to work at once, even while you sleep.
Body systems work together. When you run, your muscles need more oxygen, so you breathe faster (respiratory) and your heart beats faster (circulatory), all controlled by your brain (nervous).
Muscles can only pull, not push. That is why they work in pairs: one muscle bends your elbow, another straightens it.
Which system carries the oxygen from your lungs to your toes?
The heart pumps the blood through blood vessels.
Thinking the heart sits far over on the left. It is near the middle of the chest, tipped a little to the left, and about the size of your fist.
Going further. William Harvey discovered how blood goes around the body: Harvey: On the Motion of the Heart and Blood. Later: Body Systems Working Together in Life Science.
